name: Refrigerant pressure-temperature (saturation) tables for 22 refrigerants
cite_as: Andrii Zhukovskyi (2026). Refrigerant pressure-temperature (saturation) tables for 22 refrigerants (version 1.0.0) [Data set]. Dre Dev. https://zhukovskyi.space/calculators/hvac/refrigerant-pt-data.html
notes: Pressures are saturation pressures every 5 °F. Gauge pressure is relative to the standard atmosphere, 14.695949 psia; negative gauge values are below atmospheric pressure. A null vapor value means the source prints one column for that refrigerant, or that cell was left out. Reference data: verify against the equipment manufacturer's data before acting on it.

columns.name: safety_class
columns.description: ASHRAE Standard 34 safety class as used on the chart pages (A1, A2L, A3, B2L).

columns.name: temp_f
columns.description: Saturation temperature. One row every 5 °F, as the source charts are printed.

columns.name: temp_c
columns.description: The same temperature in Celsius, rounded to 0.01.

columns.name: liquid_psig
columns.description: Liquid (bubble point) pressure. For a refrigerant with one column this is the saturation pressure. Negative means below atmospheric pressure.

columns.name: vapor_psig
columns.description: Vapor (dew point) pressure. Empty where the source prints one column, and for the few vapor cells left out (see below).

columns.name: source
columns.description: Id of the source of the row; the sources are listed below and in the JSON file.

sources.title: Arkema Forane® Pressure-Temperature Wall Chart, Americas (2019)
Chemours, Thermodynamic Properties of Opteon™ YF, Engineering (I/P) Units
CoolProp 8.0.0, saturation pressure computed for this data set
sources.basis: Open-source property library (MIT licence); Helmholtz-energy equations of state from the literature
